steps.name: Cox model of signature score vs time-to-event
caveats: A score built on this same cohort cannot be claimed validated; the HR is an association, not a predictive claim.
If events are few, CIs will be wide — report them as they are.
steps.context: 120 samples with time and event. R 'survival' is not present in the pool; the equivalent Cox machinery is lifelines (CoxPHFitter, check_assumptions for Schoenfeld residuals) and scikit-survival (concordance, cumulative_dynamic_auc) in Python, both installed. timeROC (R) is present if a time-dependent AUC in R is preferred.
steps.question: Does the standardized 20-gene signature score associate with time to event after adjusting for condition (case vs control)?

grounding.reason: Continuous score Cox model with condition covariate and PH check per R-0153@92b8; lifelines/scikit-survival substitute for the absent R survival package

constraints: Fit a Cox proportional hazards model with the standardized signature score as a CONTINUOUS term and condition as a covariate; no median or optimized cut before the test (R-0153@92b8).
Report HR per standard deviation of the score with 95% CI, plus the condition HR.
State events, censored samples, and median follow-up before the model.
Check the PH assumption via scaled Schoenfeld residuals (lifelines proportional_hazard_test); if violated, report a stratified or time-varying model instead of a single HR.

Compute time-dependent AUC at stated horizons (choose horizons from the observed follow-up range, e.g. median and 75th percentile of event times) with scikit-survival cumulative_dynamic_auc, plus the concordance index; state the number at risk at each horizon (R-0156@9238).
Kaplan-Meier curves by score tertile for illustration only; all inference stays in the continuous model.
No penalized/gene-selection model: the 20-gene signature is fixed a priori, so R-0154 penalized-Cox machinery is not required; state that the score is not externally validated.
acceptance_criteria: Cox model table with score HR per SD (95% CI), condition HR, event/censor counts, median follow-up
PH test result with remediation if violated
Time-dependent AUC at >=2 stated horizons with C-index
KM tertile figure labeled as descriptive

Lead with the answer: is the score associated with time-to-event adjusted for condition, and how strong (HR per SD, CI, AUCs).
acceptance_criteria: Report file with all figures/tables and reproducibility record

plan.title: 20-gene signature score vs survival in case-control cohort
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is whether the study's 20-gene signature score associates with time-to-event after accounting for case vs control status (60 vs 60, unpaired, single batch, Salmon gene-level counts). Plan: (1) sample-structure QC on the raw counts with blind vst/PCA to catch outliers before any test; (2) a minimal low-count filter so the signature genes that survive are scored on a stable expression scale; (3) per-sample UCell rank-based scoring of the 20-gene signature on log-normalized expression, reporting how many signature genes are present in the matrix; (4) a Cox proportional hazards model of time-to-event with the standardized signature score as a continuous term and condition as a covariate, PH-checked via Schoenfeld residuals, with time-dependent AUC at stated horizons and Kaplan-Meier tertile curves as illustration only; (5) a reproducibility report.

steps.method: vst blind + PCA + sample distance heatmap
UCell rank-based signature scores per sample
Cox proportional hazards model on per-sample score with condition covariate
